title: Post-quantum cryptography (Kyber, Dilithium)
summary: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) provides security against quantum computers. NIST standardized: Kyber (ML-KEM, key encapsulation), Dilithium (ML-DSA, signatures), SPHINCS+ (SLH-DSA, hash-based signatures). Kyber uses module lattices (LWE problem). Dilithium uses module lattices (SIS problem). SPHINCS+ uses hash trees (no lattice assumption).

structure.meaning: Key Encapsulation Mechanism. Public key (1184 bytes for Kyber-768), ciphertext (1088 bytes), shared secret (32 bytes). Based on module-LWE.
Digital signature. Public key (1952 bytes), secret key (4000 bytes), signature (3293 bytes). Based on module-SIS.
Hash-based signature. Public key (32-64 bytes), signature (7856-49856 bytes). No lattice assumption (only hash security).
Level 1 = AES-128 (128-bit), Level 3 = AES-192 (192-bit), Level 5 = AES-256 (256-bit).
Combine PQC with classical crypto (e.g., X25519 + Kyber) for defense in depth during transition.

notes: NIST standardized ML-KEM (Kyber), ML-DSA (Dilithium), SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+) in 2024.
Kyber is used in TLS 1.3 (X25519Kyber768Draft00) and Signal Protocol.
PQC keys and signatures are much larger than classical (Kyber public key: 1184 bytes vs X25519: 32 bytes).
Post-quantum migration is the biggest cryptographic transition in history.
Hybrid mode (classical + PQC) is recommended during the transition period.
